rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause requirement
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written termination notice. Just cause is either at-fault cause (such as nonpayment of rent, material lease breach, nuisance, criminal activity) or no-fault cause (owner or family move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, compliance with a government order, or intent to demolish or substantially remodel).
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy (or 24 months for one tenant if adult tenants were added)
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property where the tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied it for 12 months; if additional adult tenants are added before an existing tenant reaches 24 months, it applies only if all tenants have 12 months or more or one or more tenants have 24 months or more. Excludes the listed exempt property types.

rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; housing in nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care and residential care facilities; school and higher-education dormitories; housing where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen with an owner who lives there; single-family owner-occupied residences (owner rents no more than two units or bedrooms, or a mobilehome); owner-occupied two-unit properties where neither unit is an ADU or JADU; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years unless a mobilehome; separately alienable property not owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, when the required exemption notice was given; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income households.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply renders the written termination notice void. An owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, reasonable attorney's fees and costs in the court's discretion, and up to three times actual damages plus possible punitive damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct; the Attorney General and city attorney or county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: (A) Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act no-fault relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the owner must either make a direct relocation payment or waive in writing the final month's rent, equal to one month of the tenant's rent in effect when the notice was issued; any relocation payment must be provided within 15 calendar days of service of the notice. The termination notice must tell the tenant of the right to relocation assistance or rent waiver.
rules.key_value: One month of the tenant's rent in effect when the notice was issued
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies for which just cause is required under subdivision (a), when the owner issues a termination notice based on a no-fault just cause, regardless of the tenant's income.

rules.penalty: An owner's failure to strictly comply renders the notice of termination void.
rules.quoted_span: The amount of relocation assistance or rent waiver shall be equal to one month of the tenant’s rent that was in effect when the owner issued the notice to terminate the tenancy.
rules.interaction_text: (C) The relocation assistance or rent waiver required by this subdivision shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act notice of tenant rights
rules.requirement: Owners of residential real property subject to the section must give tenants a notice, in no less than 12-point type, stating that California law limits rent increases and requires a statement of cause to terminate a tenancy; for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after July 1, 2020, it goes in the lease, an addendum, or a signed written notice.
rules.coverage_text: Owners of residential real property subject to Section 1946.2.
